Oral forms generally taken with water; follow local product labelling

summary: Caroverine is a quinoxaline-derived antispasmodic that acts as a non-specific calcium channel blocker and NMDA (glutamate) receptor antagonist. It is used in some countries as a smooth-muscle spasmolytic and, in specialist ENT practice, by intravenous infusion for cochlear (glutamate-mediated) tinnitus. It is not FDA-approved; dosing and indications follow regional product information.
indications: Symptomatic relief of smooth-muscle spasm (gastrointestinal, biliary, urinary - per regional labelling)
Adjunctive treatment of cochlear-synaptic tinnitus (specialist ENT use, where approved)

dosage.n: Per regional product information; not FDA-defined

dosage.d: Approximately 40-160 mg by slow IV infusion

admin: Take oral doses with water as directed by the local product information
Intravenous caroverine must be given slowly by a clinician, with blood pressure monitoring
Follow the regionally approved labelling, as this drug is not FDA-approved
moa: Caroverine acts as a non-specific (T- and L-type) calcium channel blocker producing smooth-muscle relaxation, and as a competitive NMDA-type glutamate receptor antagonist. The latter underlies its proposed use in cochlear-synaptic tinnitus, where excess glutamatergic transmission at inner hair cell-afferent synapses is implicated.
preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; use is not recommended. Caroverine is not FDA-approved and pregnancy data are lacking.
lact: Safety during breastfeeding has not been established; avoid or discontinue breastfeeding during use.
renal: No established dose adjustment; specific renal data are limited - use with caution.
hepatic: No established dose adjustment; specific hepatic data are limited - use with caution.

interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction described

counsel: May cause drowsiness or dizziness - avoid driving until effects are known
Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine
Tell your clinician about other sedative medicines you take
This medicine is not FDA-approved; follow the dosing on your local product information
pk: IV: effect within minutes; oral spasmolytic effect within ~30-60 minutes
Several hours; oral dosing typically three times daily
Store per product label, typically below 25 C, protected from light
pearls: Not FDA-approved; available in some European/Asian markets - dosing and indications follow EMA/regional product information and BNF-type sources rather than US labelling
Dual mechanism (calcium channel blockade + NMDA antagonism) explains both antispasmodic and anti-tinnitus uses
IV use for cochlear tinnitus is a specialist ENT intervention and can lower blood pressure
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose - do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may cause marked drowsiness, dizziness and hypotension. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with monitoring of blood pressure and consciousness.
